parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Translate a promise into observable claims
parts.body:
'Helpful and safe' gives a release committee nothing to decide. State the task population, user, system configuration, expected outcome, and consequence of failure. Then separate measures of task capability, factual support, privacy and security, latency, cost, and business result. A model can answer test questions well while an application retrieves the wrong document or sends information to the wrong employee. Evaluate the complete workflow.

For each claim, define a measurement method and a threshold before examining candidate results. An employee knowledge assistant might require source-supported answers on a held-out set, correct access filtering, and a human fallback on missing or conflicting policy. The percentages depend on the harm of a wrong answer and the organisation's tolerance; they are decisions to document, not universal industry numbers. Severe permission failures may block launch even if average answer quality passes.

A CAIO asks what the evidence supports at each stage. A supervised pilot with every answer checked has a different exposure from a broad, unattended release. Record the intended stage, number and mix of cases tested, unresolved failure modes, accountable approver, and date of re-evaluation.

example.title: A testable release claim
example.body: For employees in one pilot unit, the assistant cites the applicable current policy for routine leave questions and sends ambiguous cases to HR. It cannot expose another employee's restricted record. The release packet records exact thresholds, results, sample counts, and the reviewer who may pause the pilot.

exercise.title: Turn adjectives into checks
exercise.body: Take a proposal that calls an assistant 'accurate, safe, and fast.' Write the supported task, affected users, baseline, three separate test methods, severe failure rule, decision maker, and permitted launch stage. Explain what evidence would block scaling.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Map, Measure, Manage

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Build a gate that joins several measures
parts.body:
A release gate contains more than an overall score. Define hard stops for severe failures, minimum performance by important task slice, and operating constraints such as latency and cost. Specify how many cases are needed to make the evidence credible and report uncertainty. On a sample of 20, one failure changes the observed rate by five percentage points; a score of 95% does not establish the same thing as 950 successes out of 1,000. Avoid false precision from small sets.

Write the decision rules before the team tunes the system. For example, zero observed cross-user data exposures in a designed safety set may be a pilot condition. It does not prove the true probability is zero. Require negative tests, access-control inspection, production monitoring, and a plan for immediate containment. If two quality measures conflict, tell the committee which takes priority and why.

Assign ownership. The product leader owns the benefit and workflow; risk and privacy owners assess their controls; engineering owns technical reliability; the CAIO reconciles the evidence and decision packet. A committee can then approve a bounded pilot, request remediation, or decline release with a written reason.

example.title: A filled gate packet
example.body: Illustrative pilot gate: at least 90% supported answers overall, at least 95% in high-impact leave cases, no observed restricted-document exposure in the designed safety set, p95 latency at most 10 seconds, and cost at most $0.60 per accepted task. The candidate produces 170/200 supported answers (85%), including 54/60 high-impact cases (90%); one of 30 access tests leaks a restricted document; p95 is 8 seconds and cost is $0.45. The observed 85% is a sample estimate with uncertainty, and even 0/30 leaks would not prove a zero underlying risk. This candidate fails three gates, so broad release is denied. A supervised, read-only diagnostic pilot may continue only if the access fault is contained and the risk owner separately approves that bounded scope. All values are teaching assumptions.

exercise.title: Write the release decision
exercise.body: Define a held-out task set, per-slice quality threshold, access-control blocker, latency ceiling, cost budget, and human review condition for a knowledge assistant. Show counts as well as percentages. State who approves the pilot and what changes before broad deployment.

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Keep evidence tied to the tested configuration
parts.body:
An evaluation result belongs to a particular combination of model, prompt, retrieval index, tools, policy, users, and test data. Record those versions and the evaluation date. A supplier model update, a new data source, or a change from read-only to write authority can invalidate part of the evidence. The release process should identify which changes require a full gate and which need a targeted regression suite. NIST's AI RMF Core connects mapping the use context, measuring risk, and managing it through the life cycle; the local release rules still need owners and thresholds.

Maintain a concise assurance record: intended use, out-of-scope uses, owners, risk tier, tests, results by slice, known limitations, approved operating controls, monitoring signals, and next review. Link failures to remediation work. If a pilot changes geography, test the new languages, policies, and permissions; results from one region cannot silently cover another. A Canadian provincial policy and an EU employee context may differ even when the interface looks identical. The relevant policy owner must verify the applicable rule.

The record should help an operator make a decision, not just satisfy an audit. A rollback owner needs to know which threshold was breached, how to disable the feature, and who handles affected cases. Keep evidence accessible under the organisation's retention and access rules to the people with authority to act.

example.title: A material change
example.body: The pilot answered read-only questions from a curated HR corpus. A new release adds an employee-record update tool. Earlier answer-quality tests remain informative, but they do not establish safe write behaviour. The team adds authorisation, duplicate-write, and recovery tests before requesting approval.

exercise.title: Create an evidence register
exercise.body: For one proposed AI workflow, list system components and versions, tested user population, test-set date, approved scope, unresolved risks, monitoring owner, and five changes that would trigger re-evaluation. Include a regional expansion case.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: governance and monitoring

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Run a defensible scale decision
parts.body:
At the end of a pilot, compare the pre-agreed claims with measured outcomes. Show the baseline and test population, not just a vendor score. Separate observed task success from a business outcome such as handling time or service quality. Report incidents, human corrections, cost per accepted task, and where test coverage is thin. State whether pilot supervision reduced exposure and whether those controls remain at scale.

Offer a decision with scope. Expand to a named group, repair and retest, continue a bounded pilot, or stop. If expanding, specify new volume and regions, monitoring cadence, human fallback, incident threshold, and next decision date. Record dissent on unresolved material risk rather than rounding it into an average.

A CAIO should be able to tell the executive committee exactly what it is buying with a release: a measured improvement for certain tasks under stated controls. When evidence is weak, fund the missing test or redesign the workflow before raising exposure.

example.title: A bounded expansion
example.body: An assistant handles routine status queries well but has only six tested account-access cases and no tested French-language cases. The committee expands routine status coverage in the original unit, keeps account access with staff, and requires new tests before serving a bilingual region.

exercise.title: Draft the decision memo
exercise.body: Write one page for a hypothetical pilot with baseline, pre-agreed gates, results and denominators, severe failures, limitations, recommended scope, accountable approvers, monitoring triggers, and a date for the next decision. Make invented results explicit.
